dedupe_keys.name: heat network zoning in england national zoning model and 28 pilot towns and cities

description: This case study is the UK Government's heat network zoning programme for England, described on a GOV.UK collection by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero. Zoning designates areas where district heat networks are expected to be the lowest-cost route to decarbonising heat, so that local communities can accelerate network development. The Energy Act 2023 provides the powers to implement zoning through regulations, government consulted on further detail and published its response in January 2026, and a national zoning model identifies heat network opportunity areas using building type, size and existing energy use. The model was tested and refined with pilot projects in 28 English towns and cities, and some of these areas are being progressed as the first zones, with details in market engagement webinar recordings. The collection also links the 2022 and 2023 consultations, a factsheet, social research and promotional resources. Access: web pages and documents, free; the page footer states the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: a policy programme with regulations not yet in force when read, and zone maps are not shown on the page. It suits planning and policy evaluation studies of district heating expansion, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
